brief: BofA frames the week around Treasury Secretary Bessent's "I am the house now" remark: a sharp global rate selloff plus an underwhelming buyback rollout says a bigger house may be needed. US rates bear-flattened as payrolls and PPI beat, and now track oil rather than data. BofA economists forecast 0.22% core CPI, which lifts core PCE to 3.4% YoY and clears the bar for a September hike the market prices near 70%, so the larger reaction belongs to a soft print. BofA stopped out of its long 5y UST, keeps a long duration bias, and caps likely terminal pricing at 5.2%. Treasury's $6bn buyback max and at-least-$4bn guidance disappointed, driving back-end rates 5bp higher, so BofA argues issuance cuts beat buybacks (eliminating the 20y removes $574bn of 10y-equivalent supply, worth about 20bp) and stays long 30y swap spreads to -55bp. The ECB was more hawkish than BofA expected but less so than markets price, leaving the EUR front end and 10y EGB yields at the mercy of energy prices. BofA lifts its YE26 Bund forecast to 3.15%, fades nearly four priced BoE hikes, and expects a BoJ hike to 1.25%.
